{{nihongo|'''Ono Shrine (Nankoku)'''|小野神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tosa Province]].

[[File:Ono-jinja (Nankoku) torii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii]]
'''Ono Shrine''' (おのじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Koren, Okō-chō, {{ill|Nankoku, Kōchi|Q861621|qid=Q861621}}, {{ill|Kōchi Prefecture|Q134093|qid=Q134093}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The shrine enshrines the following one deity{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.
* {{ill|Prince Ametarashihiko|ja|天足彦国押人命|qid=Q11443593}} - ancestral deity of the {{ill|Ono clan|Q11464141|qid=Q11464141}}.

=== History ===
The founding date is unknown{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. Tradition says it began when the {{ill|Ono clan|Q11464141|qid=Q11464141}} that settled this area worshiped their ancestral deity{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. However, there is also a theory that the shrine name “Ono” comes from a place name rather than the clan name{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. Around the shrine are many {{ill|Kofun|Q1141225|qid=Q1141225}}, including {{ill|Koren Kofun|Q20044371|qid=Q20044371}}{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' compiled in {{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}} ({{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5), the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}}'' lists “Ono Shrine” in {{ill|Nagaoka District, Kōchi|Q1132123|qid=Q1132123}}, {{ill|Tosa Province|Q857330|qid=Q857330}}, and this is identified with this shrine{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

In the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, Ono Castle was built on the hill at the current site. It is said that when {{ill|Kagawa Chikakazu|Q3676181|qid=Q3676181}}, second son of {{ill|Chōsokabe Motochika|Q1070082|qid=Q1070082}}, returned after the decline of the Kagawa family, he was given that old Ono Castle{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. Medieval and early modern documents such as ''Nanroshi'' also contain entries calling it “Toyooka Daimyōjin,” apparently confusing it with Toyooka Daimyōjin enshrined in the precincts{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}{{Sfn|Ono Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.
